$comment: Machine-readable record of the StudioNet proof runs. Every hash here is full and unabbreviated, and every value was read back from the deployed contract rather than transcribed from a console. Re-read any of it with `genlayer call <contract> <method>`, or through genlayer-js with `node scripts/exercise-studionet.mjs <review-id> <request-tx> <review-tx>`.

signer.note: Obtained through the CLI's own BaseAction/getClient path and the OS-keychain cache populated by `genlayer account unlock`. No key was exported, no wallet or keystore was created, and no password was supplied on a command line or written to a file.

parityProof.note: Re-retrieved and re-hashed on 2026-08-22 after the second proposal lifecycle below. The contract was not redeployed at any point; both hashes still equal contractSha256. This is a claim about the contract source, not an independent audit of validator bytecode.

app.wiring: NEXT_PUBLIC_INTENT_GUARD_CONTRACT is set to the contract above, so the deployed build reads the same StudioNet state recorded in this file rather than the on-disk fixture set. The address is present in the served HTML.
app.loginWall: None. Vercel Deployment Protection was disabled on the project, so every route above answers 200 to an unauthenticated request.
app.corsVerified: https://studio.genlayer.com/api answers an OPTIONS preflight from Origin https://intent-guard-genlayer.vercel.app with access-control-allow-origin echoing that exact origin, so the browser's read path is not blocked from the deployed host.
app.serverSide: None. There is no API route, server action, database, indexer, worker or cron -- reads and writes both go from the browser straight to the GenLayer RPC, and every time transition is a permissionless button.
app.notVerified: A headless click-through of the deployed pages. The in-app browser preview on the build machine cannot attach to a remote URL, so the browser data path was verified instead by running the real genlayer-js read path against the live contract and by confirming the CORS preflight above -- not by driving the UI.

lifecycles.$comment: First proof run, 2026-08-21. Structured as an array because a second real proposal was put through the same path on 2026-08-22; both are recorded in full rather than the newer one replacing the older.

transactions.note: One DISAGREE, one IDLE and one non-fatal validator ERROR are recorded exactly as they occurred. The round still finalized and the leader's execution was SUCCESS; nothing here is smoothed over.

storedState.$comment: Read back with `genlayer call 0x971406b8F8efFA474F19657d7e55549A17e2b157 get_review --args IG-PROOF-1`. Re-read on 2026-08-22 through genlayer-js and unchanged.

is_vetoed.note: The mandate was too vague to authorise or exclude what the calls do.

verdict.why: Two of the seven actions could not be named: action #3 has selector 0x76ef8453 and action #4 carries an opaque nested payload with selector 0x00000000. The contract's own rule is that an otherwise-aligned proposal containing an opaque call is UNDERSPECIFIED, not ALIGNED, so the round declined to clear it and declined to veto it.
verdict.consequence: This proves the PENDING -> UNDERSPECIFIED path with a real bond, real validators and a real mainnet proposal. It does not prove the veto path, because this proposal did not diverge. See notProvenOnChain.

lifecycles.$comment: Second proof run, 2026-08-22, on a different real Uniswap proposal with a different action shape (9 actions, cross-chain relays) to show the path is not tuned to one input.
lifecycles.mandateTitle: [RFC] Update Crosschain Governance Parameters for Avalanche, MegaETH, Soneium, and X Layer

transactions.note: One DISAGREE again, on a round with no failed executions at all. Recorded because a unanimous round would be the surprising result: these validators fetch mainnet calldata independently and decode it under inference.

storedState.$comment: Read back on 2026-08-22 with `node scripts/exercise-studionet.mjs IG-PROOF-2 <request> <review>`, which reads through genlayer-js rather than the CLI.

get_review.mandate_title: [RFC] Update Crosschain Governance Parameters for Avalanche, MegaETH, Soneium, and X Layer

is_vetoed.note: The mandate was too vague to authorise or exclude what the calls do.

verdict.why: The round named seven of the nine actions against the mandate's own text -- actions #0 and #7 as the LayerZero trusted-remote writes for the MegaETH executors, #1/#2/#8 as OmnichainProposalSender relays, #3-#6 as bridge deposits targeting the CrossChainAccount -- and then refused to clear it, because the nested payloads inside the relay and deposit calls are opaque. Its own words: 'the specific instructions being relayed to the remote chains cannot be verified. Per rule 5 ... the verdict is UNDERSPECIFIED.'
verdict.consequence: A second real proposal, a different action count and a different call shape, reaching the same PENDING -> UNDERSPECIFIED path. It did not diverge, so per instruction the veto/rebuttal/override branches were not driven from it -- forcing a DIVERGENT verdict out of a non-divergent proposal would have been fabrication.

stats.$comment: Read live on 2026-08-22 with `stats()`. Reviews is 2, one per lifecycle above.
stats.balanceNote: `balance` is 0 after two complete lifecycles because both reviews settled and both 0.001 GEN bonds were paid back to the requester. The contract holds no stranded value, and the figure staying at 0 across a second lifecycle is itself the check -- a settlement that had silently failed to pay out would have left a balance behind.

controls.name: stock-CLI payable control
controls.observation: The same request_review submitted through the unpatched `genlayer write` reached consensus status ACCEPTED while its GenVM execution reverted, and `stats.reviews` stayed 0.
controls.why: `genlayer write` hardcodes `value: 0n`, so the bond never arrived and the contract correctly refused the call. Recorded because it is the cleanest available demonstration that consensus status is not application success.

toolingNote.limitation: GenLayer CLI 0.39.2 `genlayer write` hardcodes `value: 0n` and has no option for `gl.message.value`. `--fee-value` is not it -- `parseTransactionFees` assigns that to the nested `fees.feeValue`, while application value is the top-level `value` parameter of `writeContract`.
toolingNote.resolution: The payable `request_review` writes above were sent from a separate local clone of genlayer-cli at tag v0.39.2 with a one-field `--value-wei` addition that forwards the amount to the `value` parameter GenLayerJS already accepts. That clone is not part of this repository and no contract change was needed.
toolingNote.notAWorkaroundOn: Signing. The patched clone uses the same BaseAction/getClient path and the same OS-keychain cache as the stock CLI.

verifierFixes.$comment: Three genuine defects found in scripts/exercise-studionet.mjs while re-running it on 2026-08-22, recorded because they mean the earlier `verify:studionet` claim had never actually passed. All three are in the verifier, not the contract; no contract change was needed and none was made. `verify:studionet` is not part of the `npm run verify` chain, which is why CI never surfaced them.

fixes.defect: The FINALIZED assertion read `tx.status_name`, a field the RPC never sends. It fell through to the raw `status`, which is a numeric enum ordinal (7 = FINALIZED), so the check compared 7 against the string "FINALIZED" and could never pass.
fixes.fix: Read the camelCase `statusName` that genlayer-js decorates the payload with, and refuse a non-string status outright rather than stringifying the ordinal into a mismatch.
fixes.consequence: The script now exits 0 for both lifecycles above. Before the fix it exited non-zero for IG-PROOF-1 as well, so this is not a new-proof-only issue and is not presented as one.

fixes.defect: The `is_vetoed` read passed a hardcoded `["0x408ED6354d4973f66138C91495F2f2FCbd8724C3", 100n]`, so for any review id other than IG-PROOF-1 it silently reported a different proposal's veto state.
fixes.fix: Derive the pair from the review the script just read: `[review.governor, BigInt(review.proposal_id)]`, with the non-PENDING guard moved above the veto read so a missing review yields a clear error instead of a property access on null.

fixes.defect: The script read NEXT_PUBLIC_INTENT_GUARD_CONTRACT straight from process.env with no .env.local loader, while its sibling scripts/verify-schema.mjs in the same directory already had one. The commands documented in README.md and docs/SUBMISSION.md therefore threw `NEXT_PUBLIC_INTENT_GUARD_CONTRACT is not set` and exited 1 before opening a socket; they only worked in a shell that had exported the address by hand.
fixes.fix: Copied the sibling script's ten-line .env.local loader in verbatim rather than adding a dependency. Both documented commands now exit 0 exactly as written.
fixes.consequence: Recourse's scripts/exercise-studionet.mjs had the identical gap against NEXT_PUBLIC_RECOURSE_CONTRACT and was fixed the same way; both of its documented commands also exit 0 as written.

releaseRun.note: The run over the commit that introduced IG-PROOF-2, the three verifier fixes and this evidence file. Green on 2026-08-22.

auditMilestoneRun.note: Recorded separately because its npm ci step is the first to report 0 vulnerabilities in place of the 3 high-severity findings.

ci.note: CI runs on every push. The commit that adds this block is therefore validated by a later run than the releaseRun named here; that later run is the one the release tag points at. Both are stated rather than collapsing them into a single unfalsifiable claim.

notProvenOnChain: The veto path. A veto needs a live mainnet proposal whose executable calls genuinely contradict its own published text. Two real Uniswap proposals were put through the full request_review -> review path and neither diverged -- both returned UNDERSPECIFIED because of opaque nested calldata, which is the contract's own rule. A DIVERGENT verdict was not forced out of either one. Covered instead by deterministic tests in tests/direct/test_lifecycle.py, which drive DIVERGENT rounds under mocked inference over ABI bytes the test file encodes itself.
The rebuttal and governance-override branches, for the same reason -- they can only be reached from a standing veto, and no live round produced one.

A headless click-through of the deployed frontend. The public URL is recorded under `app` and every route was confirmed to answer 200 unauthenticated, but the in-app browser preview on the build machine cannot attach to a remote URL, so the UI was not driven by a script. The data path behind it was verified directly instead: the CORS preflight from the deployed origin, and the same genlayer-js reads the browser makes run against the live contract.
